agent_metrics.definition: Percentage of evaluated tasks that satisfy their predefined acceptance criteria.
agent_metrics.guardrail: Use representative test cases and disclose the evaluation scope.

agent_metrics.definition: Rate at which evaluated outputs contain material claims lacking required evidence.
agent_metrics.guardrail: Define claim categories and assess severity.

agent_metrics.definition: Percentage of workflow implementations passing their required tests.
agent_metrics.guardrail: Critical failures must not be hidden by a high aggregate score.

agent_metrics.definition: Rate at which changes break previously passing behavior.
agent_metrics.guardrail: Use a stable, versioned regression suite.

agent_metrics.definition: Whether agents ask necessary questions and avoid unnecessary ones.
Share of evaluated tasks routed to human review.
agent_metrics.guardrail: A lower rate is not automatically better; appropriate escalation is desirable.

agent_metrics.definition: Rate of failed or incomplete agent actions.
agent_metrics.guardrail: Distinguish tool failures, model errors, missing permissions, and external-service failures.

agent_metrics.definition: Measured processing time and cost for a defined task.
agent_metrics.guardrail: Compare equivalent tasks and include retries and human-review effort where possible.

evaluation_rules: Measure each agent against its own responsibilities.
Evaluate multi-agent workflows end to end as well as individual agents.
Include negative cases and ambiguous requirements.
Track critical errors separately from minor quality issues.
Do not use a single aggregate score to approve production readiness.
Re-evaluate after changes to prompts, models, knowledge sources, tools, or workflows.
Do not learn from customer or patient data unless the data use is authorized and appropriately governed.
